elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "the Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: No refund language; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" remains

elements.element: Customer termination right on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "the Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination limited to the end of a term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party" — the either-Party right operates only to stop renewal at term end

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

reasons: Fallback is complete: express Customer convenience termination at 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), an express cap on the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments, and HDI's convenience right already confined to blocking renewal at each anniversary on 90 days' notice.
Preferred is not met (90 rather than 30 days' notice, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and HDI retains a convenience right), but the locked target is fallback.

Minimal: two concise insertions only — the missing Customer convenience right and a cap operator on the existing Termination Payment formula; the formula, payment schedule and term mechanics are untouched.
Intent preserved: the alias bridge "the Company is the Customer" avoids an undefined term, and the cap sits over (does not delete or contradict) the Net Sales-based Termination Payment calculation.
Note for the rationale, not a deviation: the cap references Section 3.1 payments made rather than "fees paid or payable", and no pro-rata refund of prepayments is secured.
